subject: Clarify keystore custody and operator access for private deployment
messages:
From: Maya Singh <maya.singh@acerohealth.com>
To: nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai
Cc: James Liu <james.liu@acerohealth.com>, legal@acerohealth.com
Date: 2026-09-09T09:12:00-04:00
Subject: Clarify keystore custody and operator access for private deployment

Hi Nikhil —

We’re in the final stages of the DPA for our planned private deployment (VPC + on-prem gateway) and have a couple of open questions from legal/security to close out before we sign:

- Can you confirm the default custody model for the customer-managed keystore (CMK)? Is it strictly BYOK (Redwood never able to decrypt) or do you offer an operator-assisted option for recovery/maintenance?
- If Redwood needs temporary operator access for emergency maintenance, what are the bounds (who authorizes, duration, logging)?
- Do you provide an escrow/escrow-with-safeguards option (trusted third party or HSM-based escrow)? If so, can you send the proposed clause?
- For cross-border/data routing: will any telemetry or telemetry-derived data (latency counts, failure traces) ever include customer plaintext or key material? Our auditors want explicit language.

I attached our last DPA redline and a diagram of the planned deployment. If it helps we can do a short call — James (cc’d) is the contracting lead.

Thanks,
Maya Singh
Sr. Legal Ops | Acero Health

Attachments: ACERO_DPA_redline_v2.pdf (pdf)

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Singh <maya.singh@acerohealth.com>
Cc: James Liu <james.liu@acerohealth.com>, irene.choi@redwood.ai, kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-09T11:03:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Clarify keystore custody and operator access for private deployment

Maya —

Thanks for the clear summary and for sending the redline. High level answers below; I’ll follow up with suggested DPA wording and a short runbook excerpt attached. Happy to hop on a 30-minute call if you prefer.

1) Default custody model
   - We support BYOK where the customer holds the sole key material (Redwood has no access to private key material or plaintext). This is the default for Private deployments when customers select "Customer-managed keys".

2) Operator-assisted maintenance (break-glass)
   - Option A (customer-preferred): No operator access ever; any recovery requires customer-supplied keying material.
   - Option B (operational break-glass): Redwood can perform time-limited maintenance access under strict conditions:
       * Two-person authorization (customer ops + Redwood security approver).
       * Access sessions recorded and archived in immutable audit logs.
       * Access limited to a single pre-authorized runbook action; keys remain in HSM wrappers and are never exported as plaintext.
       * Maximum session length by policy (default 30 minutes), with immediate notification.

3) Escrow
   - We offer an escrow pathway that uses a customer-chosen escrow agent + HSM-protected key shares. We can provide clause language that defines custody, access triggers, and transfer procedures.

4) Telemetry/data exposure
   - Runtime telemetry (latency, token counts, error traces) never includes key material or customer plaintext. We can explicitly scope telemetry in the DPA: telemetry is aggregated/performance-only and excludes model input/output content unless customer opts into debug-mode logs (explicit opt-in).

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll attach a short DPA paragraph for each option (BYOK + break-glass + escrow).
- If you confirm which route Acero prefers (pure BYOK vs. break-glass vs. escrow), we’ll produce a one-page runbook and the exact legal language for insertion.

Attaching: redwood_cmk_runbook_excerpt.txt, keystore_topology_diagram.png

Best,
Nikhil Sharma
Head of Security Partnerships | Redwood Inference

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>
To: irene.choi@redwood.ai, kimberly.park@redwood.ai, priyom.das@redwood.ai
Cc: Maya Singh <maya.singh@acerohealth.com>, james.liu@acerohealth.com
Date: 2026-09-09T13:20:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Clarify keystore custody and operator access for private deployment (internal)

Team —

Looping you in to confirm language and operational controls before I send the final proposal to Acero. Below are suggested clauses I want to push into the DPA/addendum. Please flag concerns ASAP.

Proposed clause snippets (for insertion into DPA addendum):

A) Customer Keystore (BYOK)
   - "Customer retains exclusive control of cryptographic key material. Redwood shall not possess, store, or be able to derive customer private key material. All cryptographic operations using customer keys shall occur within customer-managed HSMs or customer-controlled KMS instances."

B) Break‑glass operator access (optional, customer-elected)
   - "In limited emergency circumstances, Redwood may perform maintenance using a temporary, auditable operator session provided the following conditions are met: (i) dual authorization by the customer’s designated authorizer and Redwood's Security Officer; (ii) session initiation limited to pre-approved runbook actions; (iii) session duration shall not exceed thirty (30) minutes unless extended by further mutual written authorization; (iv) all operator activity shall be logged in immutable audit records provided to the customer within 24 hours; (v) key material shall not be exported in plaintext at any time."

C) Escrow option
   - "Customer and Redwood may mutually designate an escrow agent to hold split key shares secured in FIPS 140-2/HSM modules. Escrow release requires an agreed trigger matrix and notarized joint authorization. Redwood shall not unilaterally access escrowed shares."

D) Telemetry and logs
   - "Telemetry collected by Redwood shall be limited to operational metrics and error traces and shall exclude customer PII, model inputs, and model outputs. Any debug logs that contain content must be explicitly enabled by the customer and are subject to the same retention and access controls as defined in this agreement."

Questions for legal/ops:
- Is dual authorization sufficient or do we require three-person auth for high-regulated customers?
- Can we commit to 24-hour delivery of audit logs to customer (may increase operational burden)?

I recommend we send Acero the BYOK baseline + optional break-glass addendum + escrow language so they can choose.

Thanks — please reply with comments; I’ll incorporate and send final version before EOD PST.

— Nikhil

From: James Liu <james.liu@acerohealth.com>
To: nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai
Cc: Maya Singh <maya.singh@acerohealth.com>, legal@acerohealth.com

Subject: Re: Clarify keystore custody and operator access for private deployment

Nikhil / team —

Thanks — this is helpful and aligns with what our auditors need. Acero prefers the escrow-with-shares option for now (we don’t want operator access unless absolutely necessary). Please:

1) Send the one-page runbook and the precise DPA clause language for escrow so our counsel can review.
2) Confirm that the audit log delivery SLA is 24 hours and that logs will be delivered in an immutable format (we prefer signed logs or S3-only-write buckets).
3) Include the DocuSign link for an addendum once we have the language.

If you can get the one-pager + exact clause by EOD your time we’ll try to route to counsel and sign next week.

Appreciate the quick turn.

— James Liu
Director, Contracts | Acero Health
